HISTORY AND PHYSICAL (H&P)

History:
• 23-year-old female with 4–5 day history of constant, progressively worsening midline lower-abdominal (“tummy”) pain, rated 8/10.  
• Pain located below the umbilicus, present continuously, no clear triggers or relieving factors.  
• Associated symptoms:  
  – Light pink vaginal bleeding beginning after normal period ended ~2 weeks ago (inter-menstrual/unscheduled).  
  – Occasional nausea without vomiting.  
  – Constipation for one week last week, now resolved; stools currently normal.  
  – Small amount of vaginal discharge.  
• Denies fever, chills, shoulder pain, dyspnea, syncope, dysuria, urinary frequency or urgency, hematuria, hematochezia, weight loss.  
• Last menstrual period: 2–3 weeks ago, described as normal.  
• Sexually active; last intercourse 4 days ago.  
• Contraception: etonogestrel implant (Implanon) placed 1 year ago; still experiences irregular menses.  
• Home pregnancy test performed ~1 month ago (result not explicitly stated but implied negative); none since pain began.  
• No prior pregnancies or surgeries.

Past Medical History:
• Chronic illnesses: none reported.  
• Surgical history: none.  
• Allergies: amoxicillin (reaction not specified).  
• Medications: etonogestrel implant; no others reported.  
• Social: Non-smoker, no alcohol or recreational drug use. Works as a school teacher. Lives with husband and his family. No recent travel (<1 year).  

Physical Examination:
• Tele-consultation only; no hands-on exam performed.  
• Patient appeared alert and able to converse.  
• No vital signs recorded.  
• No abdominal, pelvic, or systemic examination findings documented.

Impression:
Acute lower-abdominal and pelvic pain with light inter-menstrual bleeding – etiology undetermined. Must rule out pregnancy-related pathology.  
Consistent differential considerations (per transcript and reasoning):  
1. Ectopic pregnancy – reproductive age, pain + light bleeding, contraception failure possible.  
2. Pelvic inflammatory disease – lower abdominal pain, discharge/bleeding, sexually active.  
3. Ovarian cyst complication/torsion – constant severe pelvic pain, possible light bleeding.

Management Plan:
• Arrange urgent face-to-face clinic visit for abdominal and pelvic examination.  
• Perform urine pregnancy test today; patient to call back immediately if positive.  
• Safety-net advice: seek urgent evaluation sooner if pain worsens, develops vomiting, cannot keep fluids down, feels faint, or experiences heavy bleeding.  
• Contact Babylon support line to book in-person appointment.  
• No medications started during tele-visit.  
• No further tests ordered pending in-person review.

Patient Summary:
23-year-old woman with several days of worsening constant lower-abdominal pain and light post-menstrual bleeding. Pregnancy-related pathology (including ectopic) high on differential; in-person exam and repeat pregnancy test arranged.

Key Takeaways:
• Do a urine pregnancy test today and report result immediately.  
• Call support line now to schedule same-day/next-day face-to-face assessment.  
• Go to emergency care if pain escalates, heavy bleeding occurs, or you become dizzy or unable to drink.

Next Steps:
• Clinic visit for abdominal and pelvic examination, vital signs, and point-of-care pregnancy test.  
• If pregnancy test positive or ectopic suspected, urgent gynecology referral and pelvic ultrasound.  
• If negative, consider STI screen, pelvic ultrasound, CBC, CRP, urinalysis based on exam findings.  
• Reassess pain control and provide appropriate analgesia at visit.

Quality checks:
• Missing expected elements: vital signs, detailed medication list (only implant documented), complete allergy reaction details, past medical conditions review, pelvis/GU exam findings.  
• No conflicts identified between transcript and DDx.  
• Transcript quality: multiple inaudible/missing words; demographic data partially redacted, but clinical content largely intact.
